bib.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis

question: Can diffusion models match or beat GANs on image sample quality by improving the architecture and adding a way to trade diversity for fidelity?
hypothesis: The gap between diffusion models and GANs stems from heavily refined GAN architectures and from GANs' ability to trade diversity for fidelity; fixing both closes it.
contributions: Architecture ablations for the diffusion UNet (more attention heads, multi-resolution attention, BigGAN up/downsampling, AdaGN) that reach state-of-the-art unconditional FID on LSUN and ImageNet 64x64
Classifier guidance: scaling gradients of a noisy-image classifier during sampling to trade diversity for fidelity
State-of-the-art class-conditional FID on ImageNet 128, 256 and 512, matching BigGAN-deep with 25 sampling steps
Guidance combined with upsampling stacks gives the best FIDs at 256 and 512

method.summary: Ablated diffusion UNet (ADM) trained with the Lsimple + lambda*Lvlb hybrid objective and learned variances, then guided at sampling time by gradients of a separately trained classifier on noisy images (ADM-G), optionally with a two-stage upsampler (ADM-U). Evaluated against GANs and other likelihood models using FID, sFID, precision and recall on LSUN and ImageNet.

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.split: entire training set used as FID reference batch

models.name: ADM (ImageNet 128)
models.architecture: UNet, 256 channels, depth 2, 64 channels per head, attention at 32,16,8, BigGAN up/downsample, AdaGN

models.name: Noisy-image classifier (ImageNet 256)
models.architecture: downsampling trunk of the UNet with attention pool at 8x8

other.note: public TFHub model at 128; own trained model at 64

training.objective: Lsimple + lambda*Lvlb hybrid with learned variances (Nichol & Dhariwal); classifier trained on same noising distribution as the diffusion model
training.batch_size: 256 (all except ImageNet 64 diffusion: 2048); classifier 1024 for ImageNet 64
training.steps: ImageNet 128: 4360K; 256: 1980K; 512: 1940K; 64: 540K; LSUN cat 200K, horse 250K, bedroom 500K; classifiers 300K-500K
training.precision: 16-bit with loss scaling; 32-bit weights, EMA and optimizer state
training.regularisation: random crops for classifier; EMA rate 0.9999
training.hardware: NVIDIA Tesla V100 (8 per machine), PyTorch
training.compute: V100-days (Table 10): ImageNet 256 ADM-G 1980K = 962 total; ImageNet 128 ADM-G 4360K = 530 total

other.ablation_setup: batch size 256, 250 sampling steps, ImageNet 128, 700K/1200K iterations

inference.decoding: 250-step sampling (ImageNet) using Nichol & Dhariwal uniform stride; DDIM with 25 steps; 1000 steps on LSUN
inference.samples: FID in the main tables computed against whole training set; sample count not stated for tables (Figure 2 uses 10k instead of 50k)

parameters.LSUN_250_step_schedule: 90, 60, 60, 20, 20 steps per fifth of the process (Table 15)

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet distance between Inception-V3 feature distributions of samples and the full training set

metrics.name: Inception Score
metrics.definition: class-distribution coverage with confident per-sample class

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.definition: fraction of model samples inside the data manifold (fidelity)

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: fraction of data samples inside the sample manifold (diversity)

eval.protocol: Metrics recomputed with one codebase from public samples or models where possible; values for DCTransformer, VQ-VAE-2, SR3, LOGAN taken from earlier papers. No seeds or significance tests.

limits: Diffusion models are slower than GANs at sampling because of multiple forward passes.
Classifier guidance is limited to labeled datasets; no strategy is given for unlabeled data.
LSUN models needed 1000 steps; a swept 250-step schedule only mostly closes the gap, and the sweep was not exhaustive.
FID and related metrics are not a perfect proxy for sample quality.
Single runs; no seeds or confidence intervals; baseline values for several models are copied from earlier papers.
